newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League's Sydney Swans has approached veteran Paul Roos to delay his retirement with a proposed special schedule through next season. The 34-year-old former Fitzroy captain, who has played 329 matches, is seen as too valuable a player to lose. Page 30.

Australian Swimming president Terry Gathercole is lobbying hard for an anti-drug campaign that will require every swimmer to provide a urine sample for testing prior to competition during the Perth world championships in January. The proposal is currently before the International Swimming Federation. Page 30.

Australian Super League's Parramatta Eels chairman Alan Overton has enlisted Super League's player recruitment manager, Peter Moore, to ensure his team keeps their identity in the event of a unified competition next year. Page 30.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Super League has made public an outline of their own proposal for a unified competition which involves a 12-team competition, following the release of the Australian Rugby League's plans yesterday. Page 48.

A resolution seeking the withdrawal of the Canberra Kookaburras from next year's AAMI Cup competition was approved 12-1 by New South Wales Rugby Union's first-division presidents. Canberra coach Kim Thurbon was confident his team met all the criteria and said the decision lay with the NSWRU itself. Page 47.

Australian swimming Olympic gold medal winners Susie O'Neill and Michelle Ford were present at the launch of a $1.5 million sponsorship deal and a four-year commitment to Australian swimming by telecommunications company Telstra. Page 47.
THE AGE

Soccer New Zealand has given its approval for an Auckland-based team to compete in Australia's Ericsson Cup national league. Soccer Australia had earlier rejected Auckland's private bid to play citing no official approval from Soccer New Zealand. Page B6.

Australia's women's junior water polo team is scheduled for a semi-final rematch with Hungary following the team's 12-5 victory over Germany in the world junior women's water polo championships in Prague. Australian coach Bruce Falson expects his team tohave the edge. Page B15.

According to Australian head swimming coach Don Talbot, drug use among international swimmers is widespread. Talbot's comments are supported by Olympic champion and current Swiss national coach Michelle Ford, who says the drug situation has not improved since the early 1980s. Page B15.
THE HERALD SUN

The world-famous Royal Melbourne composite golf course will be rearranged for the first time since it presented the 1959 Canada Cup, allowing spectators and players to enjoy the full drama of matches. The decision follows the club's consultation with the US PGA Tour organisers. Page 72.

According to high-profile Australian Football League player manager Ricky Nixon, the announcement by the Australian Taxation Office that players and clubs would be targeted comes as no surprise, as the lucrative spin-offs associated with the huge football scene warrants closer investigation. Page 78.

Australian Football League ruckman Justin Madden will officially retire today after an 18-year, 334-game career. The move was confirmed last night after Madden's financial payout was finalised between his manager, Peter Jess, and Carlton Blues chief executive Stephen Gough. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian soccer team Sydney United's president, Ivan Simic, has announced the appointment of former Socceroo David Mitchell as player-coach, and the involvement of Sydney Olympic captain David Barrett as part of an ambitious plan for the future. Page 6.

World No.1 squash player Jansher Khan will not be competing in the $30,000 Australian Open, starting in Adelaide tomorrow. Khan contacted Squash Australia earlier this week saying he had to withdraw due to an illness in the family. Page 66.

Australian Rugby League referee Paul McBlane is expected to return to the first grade to umpire the St George-Souths game this Sunday at Kogarah Oval. McBlane had been demoted for more than three months to second grade for failing to referee an adequate 10 metres. Page 72.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
